tagline: West over the sand ridges to the Pee Dee.
intro: Out of Carthage, a courthouse town in country the Scots from the Cape Fear settled, NC 24/27 runs west over the Sandhills, low rolling hills named for their coarse sandy soil, through Biscoe and Troy to Albemarle. It is 46.2 miles, a little under an hour.

Longleaf pine once covered the Sandhills, until logging nearly finished it in 1895. Nearing the Pee Dee, Horse Trough and Shelter mountains of the Uwharrie range rise on either side of the road, isolated peaks that have outlasted the weather.

moments.title: Carthage
moments.text: The Tyson & Jones Buggy Company built carts and buggies here in the late 1800s, and a local story, repeated without evidence, has the owners turning away Henry Ford.

moments.title: Troy
moments.text: The Montgomery County seat sits on a hilltop at the eastern edge of the Uwharrie Mountains, a town that got its start cutting longleaf pine for lumber and turpentine.

moments.title: Lake Tillery crossing
moments.text: The road crosses the Pee Dee on the James B. Garrison Bridge, and the older bridge the lake was to drown in the 1920s took Army bombs, cannon fire and a ton of TNT.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook, Sandhills Scenic Drive
